issues.description: The problem description first instructs to add a final (instance) Stock attribute initialized in the SealSaloon constructor, but later explicitly requires that the stock attribute must be static and shared across all SealSaloon instances. This is an internal contradiction about whether 'stock' is an instance (final) or a static class attribute. Students will be confused which design to implement (instance vs static) and may implement an instance final field that cannot be accessed by the required static methods, or implement a static field contrary to the earlier directive.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design in the problem statement: state definitively whether 'stock' is a static (class-level) attribute or a final instance attribute. If the intent is a shared stock, update the earlier paragraph to specify 'a static final Stock stock' initialized either at declaration or in a static initializer; if the intent is per-instance stock, remove the requirement that stock and related methods be static. Ensure all examples and the UML are consistent with the chosen design.

issues.description: The problem UML and the solution expect a StockIngredient constructor with signature StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template repository provides a different constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean strictValidation). This constructor-parameter mismatch means students following the problem statement (or trying to use code from examples/tests) will not find the expected three-argument constructor in the template and may be unable to instantiate objects as shown in examples or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a three-argument constructor in the template (StockIngredient(String, int, int)) to match the problem specification and solution, or update the problem statement and examples to document and require the four-argument constructor with the strictValidation boolean. Best fix: add an overloaded three-argument constructor in the template that delegates to the existing constructor (e.g., new StockIngredient(name, price, quantity, false)) so examples/tests and student expectations align.
